decisions.title: A very small food critic
decisions.situation: Sofia puts a birthday cake in front of you. Everyone waits for a photograph. You have a different artistic vision.

choices.label: Apply cake directly to face
Offer Sofia a sticky handful
Inspect this suspicious new object

result.title: The photograph survives
result.body: The cake does not. Sofia laughs so hard the first photo is mostly ceiling.

journal.text: I wore my birthday cake. Sofia kept the photograph.

decisions.title: Your name is No
decisions.situation: You decide Sofia is called “No”, because they say it so often. You introduce them to a visitor as No. No looks tired.

choices.label: Ask No for a biscuit
Ask whether their middle name is Stop
Give them their old name back

result.title: They answer to it
result.body: Sofia says no. You point out that they have just said their own name. The visitor needs a moment.

journal.text: I named Sofia No, then asked No for a biscuit.

decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Sofia points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Sofia keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Sofia a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: The rules have been updated
decisions.situation: You are losing a board game with Sofia. You have just remembered a rule under which you would be winning.

choices.label: Finish under the original rules
Suggest your rule for the next game
Insist it has always been the rule

result.title: A respectable defeat
result.body: Sofia wins this round. You immediately request another.

journal.text: I finished a board game fairly even though I was losing.

decisions.title: The staffroom boss fight
decisions.situation: You copied your school map from a video game. Sofia wants to know why the staffroom is labelled “FINAL BOSS” and the toilets contain treasure.

choices.label: Replace the monsters with actual rooms
Ask whether the staffroom really is off limits
Insist the treasure is in the toilets

result.title: A less dangerous school
result.body: You redraw the map. The dragon becomes the library. Sofia marks the corrected version and circles the one staircase you accidentally kept.

journal.text: I replaced a video-game map with a real map of my school.

decisions.title: A nose for music
decisions.situation: Sofia has learned to play the recorder with their nose. They ask you to accompany their debut. The first note makes everyone check for a trapped bird.

choices.label: Drum on the desk and let them have their moment
Offer to be the audience from further away
Announce that you can play an imaginary one

result.title: A very short tour
result.body: You find a beat that nearly matches the squeaks. Sofia attempts an encore, sneezes, and announces an interval.

journal.text: I accompanied Sofia’s nose-recorder debut by drumming on a desk.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

choices.label: Build an elaborate fort
Read by the window
Declare the whole day ruined

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Sofia plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of
Trade one song each
Give a brutally concise review

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Sofia.

journal.text: I listened to Sofia’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: Little Star, big photograph
decisions.situation: Your school-photo proof arrives. You wore an old top that barely fits. Across your chest, in extremely clear letters, it says “LITTLE STAR”.

choices.label: Ask for a crop above the lettering
Sign the proof like a celebrity
Inspect everyone else’s proof for worse outfits

result.title: Now a very large head
result.body: The cropped proof removes the slogan and most of your shoulders. You approve it before anyone suggests keeping the original as a wallet photo.

journal.text: I cropped an embarrassing slogan out of my school photograph.

decisions.title: One star. Still hungry.
decisions.situation: Sofia Ricci (classmate) drafts a fake restaurant review of the school canteen. It includes the phrase “structural pasta”.

choices.label: Turn it into useful feedback
Keep the joke between you
Read it aloud in class

result.title: Less funny, more useful
result.body: You keep the specific complaints and remove the insults. Sofia Ferrari (teacher) helps pass it on.

journal.text: I helped Sofia Ricci (classmate) turn a canteen rant into useful feedback.

decisions.title: Selective honesty
decisions.situation: Sofia has marked a correct answer wrong and a wrong answer right. The mistakes cancel out. You could mention both, or suddenly become very interested in only one.

choices.label: Point out both mistakes
Get the answers explained properly
Ask for the lost marks. Hide the free ones.

result.title: No profit, better reputation
result.body: Sofia corrects both marks and thanks you for being honest. Your grade stays exactly where it was.

journal.text: I showed Sofia two marking mistakes that cancelled each other out.

decisions.title: Your name on the cover
decisions.situation: Sofia Ricci (classmate) asks you to share a class project. Sofia Ferrari (teacher) has given you two months. That sounds like a problem for Future You.

choices.label: Promise to write your section
Ask to work separately
Admit you cannot commit

result.title: Future You has been notified
result.body: You agree on a section to write. The deadline is saved; agreeing has not completed any work.

journal.text: I agreed to write a section of a class project with Sofia Ricci (classmate).

decisions.title: The project is due
decisions.situation: Sofia is putting the class project together. Sofia wants your section today. The blank page has enjoyed two months of peace.

choices.label: Finish your section
Ask Sofia for help
Leave your section blank

result.title: Your name belongs on it
result.body: You finish your section and explain it to Sofia. Sofia records the work you actually did.

journal.text: I finished my section of the class project with Sofia.

decisions.title: At least you know your name
decisions.situation: Your practice exam is going badly. So far, you have written your name and the date. The date is wrong.

choices.label: Hunt for every easy mark first
Take the wreckage to Sofia afterwards
Write an apology in the answer box

result.title: A rescue in small pieces
result.body: You collect enough answers to get moving. Even question one looks less hostile on your second visit.

journal.text: I recovered from freezing in a practice exam by answering easier questions first.

decisions.title: A promise remembered
decisions.situation: Two years after that class project, Sofia Ricci brings it up. Back then, you finished your section.

choices.label: Remember doing your part
Tell Sofia it does not matter
Leave it in the past

result.title: An old project, an honest conversation
result.body: You acknowledge that you finished your section. Sofia hears you out.

journal.text: I talked honestly with Sofia about our old project, when I finished my section.

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: One more attempt at your name
decisions.situation: At a local discussion group, the host mispronounces your name twice and then suggests a nickname you have never used.

choices.label: Say your name clearly once more
Turn the correction into a light joke
Use the nickname for the afternoon

result.title: A manageable correction
result.body: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.

journal.text: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

decisions.title: The sofa is judging you
decisions.situation: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
Invent a chair-based version
Keep up with him at full speed

result.title: An achievable number of elbows
result.body: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.

journal.text: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality
Disclose that you eat cabbage
Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: Evidence from a previous haircut
decisions.situation: Sofia sends you an old photograph. The haircut is difficult to defend. The memory attached to it is much better.

choices.label: Ask for the whole story
Save a copy and label it
Focus entirely on the haircut

result.title: An unreliable defence witness
result.body: Sofia remembers the day fondly, then admits thinking the haircut was a good idea. You forgive the first part.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Sofia also confessed to approving the haircut.

decisions.title: The accidental millionaire
decisions.situation: At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Admit your wealth has been exaggerated
Donate €224.75 to the donkey charity
Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

result.title: A donkey-sized misunderstanding
result.body: You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
Follow the trolley out
Perform an increasingly furious dance

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: You said that part out loud
decisions.situation: You rehearse a devastating comeback while walking. A stranger turns around just as you announce, “That is why nobody trusts your ferret.”

choices.label: Explain that you were arguing in your head
Write the useful point down privately
Pretend to be on an important phone call

result.title: No actual ferret dispute
result.body: The stranger accepts the explanation and walks on a little faster. You retire the argument before it recruits anyone else.

journal.text: I stopped an imaginary argument after saying part of it aloud.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: Doing nothing, attendance required
decisions.situation: You put “Do absolutely nothing” in your calendar. The app sends invitations to a discussion group. Six people accept and one asks about the dress code.

choices.label: Cancel it and protect your hour
Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution

Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

Identify every interruption

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Milan.

decisions.title: Not the tabletop version

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

Cover the portrait and leave

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.
